court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court, Erode, HMOP No. 1 of 2014
case_name: K. Shanmugha Raja @ Raja vs Shanthakumari
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2003. The respondent frequently deserted the matrimonial company and there was no consummation between them. The appellant sought dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib)(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage between a Hindu and a person who belongs to a different religion, even if it is solemnised by following Hindu rites and customs, is void.
legal_principles.held: wherein it was held that a marriage between a Hindu and a person who belongs to different religion, even if it is solemnised by following Hindu rites and customs, is void.
cited_cases: Gullipilli Sowria Raj vs. Bandaru Pawani @ Gullipilli Pawani, (2009) 1 Supreme Court Cases 714

legal_principles.principle: Even if a plea is not specifically made, a party can still rely on it if it is satisfactorily proved by evidence.
legal_principles.held: then the mere fact that the plea was not expressly taken in the pleadings would not necessarily disentitle a party from relying upon, if it is satisfactorily proved by evidence.
cited_cases: Bhagwati Prasad vs. Shri Chandra Maul, AIR 1966 SC 735
use_in: cases involving alternative claims or implied issues

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the original petition filed by the appellant for dissolution of marriage is allowed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
